subject: BYO KMS coverage questions + audit/retention prioritization
messages:
From: Susan Kim <susan.kim@novahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>; marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2026-10-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — BYO KMS + retention requirements

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team appreciated seeing the Dedicated flow. A few immediate clarification requests from our security and procurement leads before we move forward:

- KMS coverage: we need a clear statement of which logs/keys are encrypted with customer-managed keys vs platform keys (audit logs, access logs, metrics exports). Can you provide a mapping?
- Retention windows: what flexibility do we have per-tenant? NovaHealth needs 7 years for specific audit records, but shorter for session telemetry.
- Rotation policy: is there a supported key rotation handoff? What is the expected ops involvement?

We’d like a short one-pager and an example timeline to share with legal/procurement. Can you send by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Susan Kim
Director, Information Security
NovaHealth

Date: 2026-10-04T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — BYO KMS + retention requirements

Susan — thanks for the concrete asks. Looping in Marissa (product), Grace (security), Ben (sales ops), and Karthik (infra) to give one consolidated answer.

Quick plan: we’ll draft a short coverage matrix and a proposed retention mapping plus two implementation options for long-term retention (native retention vs. archival export to S3 under customer key). Questions for you while we prep:

1) Which specific audit record types are in scope for the 7-year requirement (API audit, user auth, model inference audit trail, payload redaction events)?
2) Do you need continuous access to those records or just on-demand export for audits?

We’ll target a working doc by 10/06 and a slide-ready one-pager by 10/08.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Susan Kim <susan.kim@novahealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — BYO KMS + retention requirements

Folks — I pulled together two alternative flows and attached a draft mapping (audit-schema-proposal.yaml) + a proposed mutual action plan. High level notes:

- Coverage matrix (attached):
  * API request logs: platform supports encrypt-at-rest; customer-provided CMKs are supported for encryption of archived exports only.
  * Inference payload traces: optionally stored; default redaction applied. If NovaHealth mandates full payload retention, we recommend archival to customer S3 encrypted with your CMK.
  * Auth and access logs: currently captured by platform and can be exported nightly; we can offer a TTL option up to 7 years via export/archival.

- Rotation and key handoff: we support scheduled re-wrapping of exported archives and have a documented key-roll process. Live keys used by runtime are platform-managed with an HSM; we offer an enterprise KEK binding for Dedicated Private mode where runtime can use a customer-wrapped key under strict audit.

Open engineering questions for Karthik/infra: can we commit to a documented playbook for on-prem key injection and automated monthly rotation without requiring a maintenance window? If not, we should flag the exception and offer an S3-only archival fallback.

Next steps I propose:
1) Grace & Karthik validate the coverage statements and list tech constraints.
2) Jonas confirms compliance wording for the contract one-pager.
3) Ben coordinates with NovaHealth procurement on whether they require continuous access or export-on-request.

Attaching: audit-schema-proposal.yaml, redwood-byo-kms-coverage-proposal.pdf

-Marissa
Sr Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Susan Kim <susan.kim@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — BYO KMS + retention requirements

Thanks Marissa — reviewed the attached mapping. Quick technical clarifications from security:

- We should be explicit about the difference between "audit logs" and "inference telemetry" in legal language. They carry different PII/PHI risk profiles and different retention justifications.
- For Dedicated Private customers, we can offer a runtime KEK binding as an alpha capability; it requires a short playbook change to wire the runtime to a customer KEK in KMS. That binding currently requires a manual step at deploy time.
- Rotation without a maintenance window: we can support rewrapping of archived objects asynchronously. For live runtime key rotation we need a short (sub-10m) rolling restart unless we deliver an in-memory rewrap hook (engineering effort Q1).

I think two escalation points to surface to Procurement: 1) the small operational window for live-key rotation; 2) the archival/export model being the recommended approach for 7-year retention to avoid runtime constraints.

On my side I’ll draft the short technical caveats to include in the one-pager.

-Grace
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-06T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — BYO KMS + retention requirements

Quick infra check from my side after a short spike:

- We can offer two delivery patterns:
  Option A (recommended): nightly export of scoped audit artifacts to customer S3 buckets encrypted with customer CMK. No runtime changes, supports arbitrary retention windows, and plays nicely with NovaHealth's long-term retention policy.
  Option B: runtime KEK binding for Dedicated Private (alpha): requires deploy-time injection and a small rolling restart during key rotation. Possible to automate further but will take Q1 engineering cycles to remove the restart requirement.

- Implementation detail: export schema will include a hash index to allow replay and selective recall; we’ll include a minimal index in the export that contains timestamp, record type, tenant id, and object pointer. We attached a sample schema (audit-schema-proposal.yaml).

Action items:
- Marissa: include Option A as the default commercial commitment and Option B as an enterprise add-on with explicit operational caveats.
- Jonas/Grace: list the exact audit types we will include in nightly exports.
- Ben: schedule follow-up with NovaHealth procurement next week to confirm export access patterns and tagging requirements.

I’ll follow up with a short runbook for deploy-time KEK injection.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
